title: Security governance program for self-hosted infrastructure

problem.description: A fully self-hosted development and operational infrastructure — an Arch Linux workstation, multiple repositories, Docker servers, local AI agents with MCP tools — grows without an explicit threat model. Key questions remain unanswered in documented form: who can confer authority to an agent, which boundaries separate processes, where secrets live, how to prove a control actually works. The answer cannot be 'install a scanner': it takes a documentary foundation with a declarative inventory, repeatable audits, and a findings register with tracked lifecycle state.
painPoints: No explicit threat model for AI agents with access to filesystem, Docker and Git
Local API surfaces (self-hosted control plane, MCP tools) without verified authentication/authorization
No canonical register of security findings: known issues not tracked with severity, state and owner
Hard to separate confirmed evidence from hypotheses when the analysis is done by an LLM

constraints.timeline: Ongoing program, foundation in 1 day + incremental audits upon authorization
constraints.budget: Documentary base with no services or scanners: zero license and dedicated infrastructure costs
technical: Read-only static code analysis: no tests, exploits or unauthorized runtime actions
Confidentiality of the material: only redacted summaries and references in the audit repository, never raw output or secrets
The LLM is not the final authority: evidence validation requires registered independent human review
Remediation scoped to the respective owning repositories, not centralized
compliance: Confidential disclosures and incidents handled via a dedicated channel (SECURITY.md)
No client or third-party data for security testing; only authorized own assets

solution.architecture: A documentary security governance program organized in four components: a declarative asset inventory (workstation, repositories, servers, sites — no scanning), a canonical findings register with monotonic IDs and a full state cycle (proposed → validated → planned → closed, with false positives and accepted risks documented), an audit archive with scope, collection plan, evidence index and report, and rules of responsibility for the AI agents involved. The first application audit (MC-MCP-001) was a read-only static review of the MCP server of the self-hosted control plane for AI agents: a 4-actor threat model, trust boundary analysis (client → guardian, environment → policy identity, manifest → child process, HTTP caller → REST API) and a security scan with a specialist model validated against an independent baseline.
keyDecisions: Documentation before tooling: declarative inventory and findings register as the base, with no services or monitors to maintain
Structural distinction between severity, evidence_state (hypothesis/confirmed) and confidence: high confidence never promotes evidence to confirmed
No automatic state transitions for findings: every transition requires registered independent review
Minimized collection approach: only redacted summaries in the repository, raw artifacts discarded; redaction is never delegated to the LLM
Audits as repeatable cases with scope, budget and stop criteria approved before execution
Remediation always in the component's owning repository, with assigned owner and tasks
solution.approach: Program foundation first, then incremental audits upon explicit authorization, each with a signed scope and stop criteria. The first step is never to launch a scanner: it is to approve the scope and the minimized collection channel.

results.impact: Program in progress. The static review showed that the control plane, in the examined state, must not be considered an independent verifier or a security sandbox: the registered findings are in proposed state, awaiting independent validation and remediation in their respective repositories. The workstation audit (ARCH-001) is planned but not yet authorized. The value today is methodological: inventory, threat model and findings register make risk discussable and traceable instead of implicit.

Registration and prioritization of findings with motivated severity and confidence
Rules of responsibility for the AI agents involved in security

code.caption: No automatic finding promotion: validation requires confirmed evidence and independent review
code.snippet:
def transition(finding, new_state, reviewer):
    # No automatic promotion: "validated" requires confirmed
    # evidence and a reviewer independent from the author.
    if new_state == "validated":
        assert finding.evidence_state == "confirmed"
        assert reviewer != finding.author
    finding.history.append((new_state, reviewer))
    finding.status = new_state
